title: Are you asking the right questions?
html:
‘To whom?’ you might be thinking. ‘To whom am I asking the right questions?’

To you!

You are the person who has to ask yourself the right questions to know what you want and to find answers to problems. Did you know that even if a question isn't directed at you, your brain will do a quick search, zoom - zang, and look for an answer?

And it's great when we get one, isn't it? How often do you watch game shows and are compelled to yell at the TV, "Come on, it's such and such, it's easy, you must know this one!" But, when the pressure is on and you have to think quickly, it's a lot harder, and this is where asking yourself the right questions will help.

So, what are the right questions? They will depend on what you do or the situation you are in. But I know that if you practice asking yourself questions when you're not under pressure, they will come to you more easily when you are.

Here are some examples to help you: ‘What is the right question to ask in this situation?’ ‘What is the desired outcome?’ ‘Has this happened before?’

These are few examples you can practice in the comfort of your own mind. Have fun with it and think of different situations where you might have to ask the right question, before you are in that situation. Even if you only do this exercise once a month, the results will surprise you.
